infrastructure: Malta has good fibre broadband and 5G coverage for its small size.
Subsea cable connections to Italy and North Africa provide international connectivity.
Small physical size limits data centre scale, though existing facilities are modern.
talent: University of Malta has limited AI research capacity, though it has an active AI research group.
Malta attracts some international tech workers through its English-language environment and EU membership.
Small population (530,000) severely constrains the domestic talent pool.
governance: Malta has established itself as a regulatory sandbox for blockchain and digital assets, demonstrating governance innovation.
GDPR compliance is in place; the IDPC (Information and Data Protection Commissioner) is the regulator.
Strong EU integration provides regulatory predictability for international AI companies.
investment: Malta's igaming and fintech sectors attract international investment that spills over into AI tools.
The Malta Digital Innovation Authority (MDIA) supports blockchain and AI innovation.
Limited domestic venture capital; international investment dominates.
economic_readiness: A services-dominated economy (igaming, tourism, financial services) with significant AI adoption in igaming analytics.
English-language environment facilitates adoption of international AI products.
Small domestic market requires internationally oriented AI businesses.
